title: General inclusion-exclusion for a finite family of decidable subsets, as two Nat sums rather than one signed one, and the two-set case is the pre-existing lemma verbatim
statement: Let A be a family of decidable subsets of the ambient range [0,m), indexed by i < n. Write ieSumPos A n m b for the sum of the cardinalities of the intersections of the NON-EMPTY subfamilies whose index set has cardinality parity b. Then the cardinality of the union plus the even sum equals the odd sum: |union| + ieSumPos true = ieSumPos false. Nat has no negatives, so the classical alternating sum is stated as this pair of Nat sums; the ungraded form ieSum true + |union| = ieSum false + m is the same identity before the empty subfamily's contribution -- exactly m, the whole ambient range -- is cancelled off both sides. At n = 2 the theorem specialises to countRange (setUnion (A 0) (A 1)) m + countRange (setInter (A 0) (A 1)) m = countRange (A 0) m + countRange (A 1) m, which is Nat.countRange_union_add_inter's statement; that specialisation is a declared theorem, not a resemblance.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Subsets.inclusion_exclusion_pos : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool))) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.add (AxNat.countRange (AxNat.Subsets.unionAt x0 x1) x2) (AxNat.Subsets.ieSumPos x0 x1 x2 Bool.true)) (AxNat.Subsets.ieSumPos x0 x1 x2 Bool.false))))
formal.kernel_statement: Nat.Subsets.meetInd A n s v := prodRangeIf s (fun i => if A i v then 1 else 0) n; Nat.Subsets.meetCard A n s m := sumRange (fun v => meetInd A n s v) m; Nat.Subsets.unionAt A n := fun v => anyOf (fun i => A i v) n; Nat.Subsets.ieSum A n m b := sumSel n (fun s => meetCard A n s m) b; Nat.Subsets.ieSumPos A n m b := sumSelPos n (fun s => meetCard A n s m) b. The ungraded form is Nat.Subsets.inclusion_exclusion : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool))) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.add (AxNat.Subsets.ieSum x0 x1 x2 Bool.true) (AxNat.countRange (AxNat.Subsets.unionAt x0 x1) x2)) (AxNat.add (AxNat.Subsets.ieSum x0 x1 x2 Bool.false) x2)))). The two-set specialisation is Nat.Subsets.inclusion_exclusion_two : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool))) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.add (AxNat.countRange (AxNat.setUnion (x0 AxNat.zero) (x0 (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero))) x1) (AxNat.countRange (AxNat.setInter (x0 AxNat.zero) (x0 (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero))) x1)) (AxNat.add (AxNat.countRange (x0 AxNat.zero) x1) (AxNat.countRange (x0 (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x1)))). The per-element identity the proof turns on is Nat.Subsets.sumSel_meetInd : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool))) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : Bool) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.Subsets.sumSel x1 (fun (x4 : ((x4 : AxNat) -> Bool)) => AxNat.Subsets.meetInd x0 x1 x4 x3) x2) (AxNat.Subsets.prodPar (fun (x4 : AxNat) => x0 x4 x3) x1 x2))))), and the product expansion's alternating law is Nat.Subsets.prodPar_even : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.Subsets.prodPar x0 x1 Bool.true) (AxNat.add (AxNat.Subsets.prodPar x0 x1 Bool.false) (AxNat.Subsets.noneOf x0 x1)))).

provenance.established_by: axeyum lane `inclusion-exclusion-mobius`, roadmap item W2-19: `nat_prelude/inclusion_exclusion.rs`. ADR-1624.
provenance.source: Classical (da Silva / Sylvester). The constructive content here is entirely in the encoding: no negatives, no Finset quotient, and no choice.

prior_art.establishes: the same theorem over an additive commutative GROUP, where the alternating sign is a ring element; this one is over Nat and therefore has to be a pair of sums, and its two-set case is the pre-existing Nat lemma

evidence.supports: the classical statement, over the non-empty subfamilies, admitted by the trusted gate with an empty axiom footprint
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.notes: The proof is `sumSel_swap` (turning the sum over subsets of a sum over elements inside out), then `sumSel_meetInd` at each ambient element, then `prodPar_even`, then `countRange_compl` to convert the residue into m minus the union's size without writing a subtraction. The graded pair is what makes the last step possible in Nat.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: Offered at a statement with the two parities exchanged -- the union's size added to the ODD sum -- and REJECTED. That is the one substitution that turns a true statement into a false one while keeping every type well-formed.

evidence.supports: the two-set case is recovered EXACTLY, and the recovery is checked by the kernel rather than asserted
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.notes: The test builds the statement ONCE and offers it to the trusted gate TWICE: once with the derived theorem and once with `Nat.countRange_union_add_inter` applied at `A 0` and `A 1`. Both are admitted, so the two are the same type -- not two similar-looking renderings that a reader would have to compare by eye. The specialisations the kernel performs unaided: `unionAt A 2 v` IS `setUnion (A 0) (A 1) v`, because `anyOf`'s base case is the literal `false` that collapses a one-element union.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: A third offer, at the same statement with `A 0` replaced by `A 1` on the right, is REJECTED. Without it the double-acceptance would be consistent with a statement so weak that anything proves it.

evidence.supports: the theorem's numbers are the right numbers at a worked three-set instance, subset by subset
evidence.notes: A i = {i, i+1} over [0,4), so A 0 = {0,1}, A 1 = {1,2}, A 2 = {2,3}. All EIGHT subset intersections are asserted separately -- 4, 2, 2, 2, 1, 0, 1, 0 -- because a meetInd that intersected the wrong subfamily can still make the totals agree. The union has 4 elements, the odd sum is 6, the even sum is 2, and 4 + 2 = 6.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: Every one of the eleven numeric assertions is paired with `expected + 1` (or the complementary Bool), so none of them can pass against a term that fails to reduce.

evidence.supports: the per-element alternating identity, which is the whole argument before it is summed over the range
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.notes: One induction on the width and one Bool dichotomy on the new element: when it is IN, the residue is multiplied by 0 and the two graded halves exchange; when it is OUT, both halves and the residue are unchanged. No hypothesis is needed at all, because the family is Bool-valued and the indicator is 0 or 1 by construction rather than by assumption.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: Offered with the residue moved to the EVEN side and REJECTED; and `meetCard_empty` is offered returning the family WIDTH instead of the ambient size and REJECTED, which is the confusion the four-argument `meetCard A n empty m` invites.

notes: epistemic_status and external_status agree: inclusion-exclusion is classical. What is not routine is the encoding. Three choices are load-bearing and each is recorded in ADR-1624: the graded PAIR instead of a signed sum (Nat has no negatives and there is no Int.sumRange toolkit at this build position); the subset as a Nat -> Bool PREDICATE instead of a Nat.Finset (two Finsets with the same members are not Eq, so the split law could not be refl); and `anyOf` as a fresh bounded existential instead of a reuse of Nat.Finset.allBelow, purely so that anyOf c 2 reduces to setUnion (c 0) (c 1) by iota and the two-set case is a corollary rather than a second argument.
